samples.summary: Untrusted `headingLevel` is interpolated unescaped into a DOCX XML attribute; this change lengthens the taint path by making the value survive a list round trip
samples.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` builds `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` with no escaping or numeric validation, even though the same file defines `escapeXmlAttr` (docx-style-map.ts:25) whose comment warns the risk is that a value can "inject attributes". `headingLevel` is only typed as `1|2|...|6`; at runtime it can be any JSON value because `deserializeClipboard` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:40-45) returns `payload.blocks as Block[]` unvalidated and `TextEditor.handlePaste` feeds it straight to `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:1228,1240). Attack: a hostile page sets the `application/x-wafflebase-docs` flavour on a copy event with a block whose `headingLevel` is the string `1"/><w:evil/><w:x w:val="`; the victim pastes, exports to DOCX, and injected WordprocessingML lands in `word/document.xml`. Before this change a pasted *list-item*'s level was destroyed (setBlockType deleted it and toggleList hardcoded 'paragraph'); now `pastedHeadingLevel` (text-editor.ts:41) forwards it, `MemDocStore.setBlockType` retains it for `list-item` (memory.ts:258-260), and `unlistedBlockType` re-applies it verbatim as the level of a real `heading` (types.ts:337-344), reaching the unescaped sink via `block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined` (docx-exporter.ts:184). Fix: clamp/coerce the level to 1..6 at the model boundary, or escape at line 96.

samples.summary: No schema validation on the internal clipboard payload, so attacker-controlled block fields (including the now-retained `headingLevel`) become model state and are written into the shared CRDT
samples.evidence: `deserializeClipboard` only checks `version === 1` and `Array.isArray(payload.blocks)`, then returns `payload.blocks as Block[]` — an unchecked cast of attacker-supplied JSON (clipboard.ts:40-48). Any page can populate the custom `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` flavour on a `copy` event, and `handlePaste` prefers that flavour over `text/html`/`text/plain` (text-editor.ts:1226-1244). With this change the pasted `headingLevel` is no longer dropped when the block is a list item, so a non-numeric or out-of-range value can be handed to `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType`, which stringifies it into the shared tree attribute (`attrs.headingLevel = String(opts?.headingLevel ?? 1)`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1386) and persists it through the backend `docs-tree` serializer. Co-editors read it back via `Number(attrs.headingLevel)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:439), yielding `NaN` — one user's paste can poison a block attribute for every collaborator and for the stored document. I could not confirm a memory-safety or code-execution consequence, only corrupted shared state plus the export-injection sink above, hence medium confidence. Recommend validating/normalizing pasted blocks (type enum, headingLevel in 1..6, list fields) in `deserializeClipboard` or `insertBlocks`.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts serialize/deserialize helpers looking for a validator/normalizer

samples.summary: Committed review-verdict artifact in the working tree asserts "approved … Nothing to report", which can steer automated reviewers of this branch
samples.evidence: .agent-review/docs/summary.md:1-3 is a checked-in reviewer output stating "✅ Docs review: **approved** — no critical or major findings" and "Nothing to report", referring to the task docs this PR adds. Any reviewer or agent reading the working tree encounters a pre-baked approval conclusion for the change under review — review-influencing content living in the repo rather than in PR discussion. I treated it as data and disregarded it. It does not appear in the diff, so it may predate this change, but branch-scoped verdict artifacts should not be committed.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. docx-style-map.ts:96 interpolates headingLevel unescaped into a double-quoted XML attribute, in a file that defines escapeXmlAttr (25-32) and applies it to the comparable untrusted fontFamily (53-56), naming attribute injection as the risk; the `number` type at line 91 is compile-time only. The value reaches the sink unvalidated: deserializeClipboard (clipboard.ts:38-49) checks only version===1 and Array.isArray(blocks), then casts `payload.blocks as Block[]`; handlePaste (text-editor.ts:1226-1244) passes it straight to insertBlocks, which copies headingLevel verbatim onto head/tail blocks (3606, 3636 via pastedHeadingLevel at 42-45, returning pasted.headingLevel unchanged for headings) and clones middle blocks with only fresh ids (3622). docx-exporter.ts:182-185 forwards block.headingLevel with no clamp. The list round-trip retention also checks out (memory.ts:249-260 preserves prevHeadingLevel for list-item; types.ts:337-344 re-applies it as a real heading level), though a directly pasted heading block reaches the sink without it. No guard makes it unreachable: clamping exists only on unrelated paths (serialize/markdown.ts:104, model/named-styles.ts:108), and the other producer (import/docx-style-map.ts:139,144) uses parseInt so cannot supply a string. Two cosmetic inaccuracies (MIME constant is application/x-waffledocs per clipboard.ts:67; cited clipboard line range) do not affect the mechanism. Unescaped interpolation of unvalidated input into generated markup is in the injection lane; I could not confirm cross-origin readability of custom clipboard flavours in every browser, which bears on exploitability but is not a refutation ground.
